sweepFindings.quote: ch27 ex04: "Rowan opens six months of storage-unit charges... Nothing in the file looks dramatic until one line repeats" | ch29 ex06: "Soraya reviews four weeks of calendar exports... Nothing dramatic happens. The telling detail is smaller" | ch32 ex01: "Gwen reviews six weeks of help-desk notes... The telling detail is not the word recovery; it is the blank line" | ch34 ex03: "Nova sorts old planning files... Nothing dramatic happens at the table. The audit shows the detail that matters"
sweepFindings.detail: The 'audit' example in four separate chapters is the SAME scene skeleton: a protagonist reviews several weeks/months of their own records (storage charges / calendar exports / help-desk notes / planning files), the narration explicitly says nothing dramatic happens, and then 'the telling detail' is one small repeated line that reveals the chapter's lesson. The phrases 'Nothing dramatic happens' and 'the telling detail' recur near-verbatim, and the requiredBeat is identical in spirit ('a record review finds the residue', 'Discovery comes from reviewing files and finding the telling detail', 'Nova reviews files and finds the repeated detail'). A reader doing all four chapters meets the identical discovery-by-records frame with only the nouns swapped. This is the most-missed class: same frame, different nouns.

sweepFindings.quote: ch27 ex06: "Apolline sits with a Saturday page divided into money, time, and attention before she opens the first drawer" | ch30 ex01: "Etienne has a Sunday evening page divided into three boxes: 45 minutes to polish a media brief, 45 minutes to review algebra, or 45 minutes to move bedtime earlier... No laptop is open yet. The whole scene is the allocation of one quiet block before Monday." | ch34 ex05: "Lorraine lays next week's calendar, a medical bill, and a Daily Stoic memento mori coin on the kitchen table. No calls have been made. No errands have started."
sweepFindings.detail: The 'planning_choice' example across ch27, ch30, and ch34 shares one frame: a protagonist sits with a page/calendar that divides time into boxes/slots, BEFORE any action begins, and must allocate 'scarce attention' — with the narration insisting no execution is shown ('before she opens the first drawer', 'No laptop is open yet', 'No calls have been made'). The requiredBeats echo each other almost word for word ('planning scene allocates attention', 'the whole scene stays inside the time allocation, with no execution shown', 'allocates scarce attention... and no execution shown'). The audience lines are near-identical ('readers allocating scarce attention before any decluttering starts' / 'readers allocating a week before action begins'). Same pre-action time-budgeting tableau, swapped props.

sweepFindings.quote: ch28 fullRead: "Put the phone in the hall, and a cheap spell breaks at once." ex03 whatToDo: "Holly leaves the phone in the hall" ex05 whatToDo: "Beau leaves the phone outside the kitchen" | ch29 ex05 whatToDo: "phone outside the room" | ch30 hook/tryThisNow: "move your phone charger outside the bedroom" ex06: "puts the phone face down" ifThenPlan: "putting the device on its charger outside the room"
sweepFindings.detail: The concrete remedy beat 'remove the phone from the room' is reused as the climactic fix across ch28 (Seek Solitude), ch29 (Be a Human Being: 'phone outside the room'), and ch30 (Go to Sleep: 'charger outside the room', 'phone face down', 'phone set across the room'). Within a single book each chapter's actionable payoff collapses to the same physical move with near-identical wording ('phone in the hall' / 'phone outside the room' / 'charger outside the room'). A reader doing the run notices the same prescription dressed three times.

sweepFindings.quote: ex02: "Tatum frowns in an adult education class as the instructor sketches Diogenes, Cynicism, Athens, and the barrel tradition" vs q02: "A training facilitator uses Socrates in the Athens marketplace during onboarding for a retail team. What should Tatum take from the case?" vs q09: "You are Tatum, writing a reflection after studying Diogenes and Cynicism in Athens"
sweepFindings.detail: Within ch27 the name 'Tatum' is used for two different people: an adult-education philosophy student (ex02, q09 reflection) and a member of a retail team in corporate onboarding (q02). These are incompatible personas sharing one name inside the same chapter — a reader cannot reconcile the philosophy-class learner with the retail onboarding trainee. Classic persona drift across sections of one chapter.

sweepFindings.quote: ex03: "finds the same line in three folders: call Lorraine when the rush ends" / q03: "the same postponed call to Lorraine" vs ex05: "Lorraine lays next week's calendar, a medical bill, and a Daily Stoic memento mori coin on the kitchen table" / fullRead: "Lorraine sees the limit while planning a week with too little time"
sweepFindings.detail: Within ch34 'Lorraine' is simultaneously (a) the offstage person Nova keeps failing to phone — the object of a neglected promise — in ex03 and q03, and (b) a full protagonist who budgets her own week and is named in the fullRead breakdown as a planner facing her own mortality filter. The same name carries two unrelated identities in one chapter, which reads as copy-paste name reuse rather than one coherent character.

sweepFindings.quote: ch28 card01 back: "You return with clearer attention, less need to perform, and more ability to meet people without heat. The return is the evidence." | ch29 card05 back: "...lets attention settle. A Being Block uses that quiet so the person returns clearer, not more withdrawn." | ch32 card01 back: "It asks what the break returned: clearer attention, kinder energy, and one next step, or fog, secrecy, and a stronger craving"
sweepFindings.detail: The lead review card in ch28, ch29, and ch32 reduces to the identical 'return test' formulation — the practice is validated by whether you 'return clearer / more available / with clearer attention.' Ch28 ('The return is the evidence'), ch32 ('A break proves itself by what it returns', 'Real rest brings you back'), and ch29 ('returns clearer') restate one template card back with synonyms. The 'clearer attention' + 'come back kinder' couplet recurs verbatim enough that the cards feel interchangeable across chapters.

sweepFindings.quote: ex03 "Rocco and Jaspreet Stop the Pitch" / fullRead "interrupts Jaspreet twice" / ex06 "a message from Rocco asks for quick feedback"; Madeline appears in ch30 fullRead, ex04, ex06 AND as the wise voice in ex05 Bonnie thread; Bonnie is Valerie's offstage 'emergency contact' in ex02 but a protagonist presenter in ex05 and q08
sweepFindings.detail: Ch30 recycles a tight name-pool (Rocco, Jaspreet, Madeline, Bonnie, Pascal, Valerie) across its examples and quiz in ways that blur identity. 'Bonnie' is a minor offstage emergency contact in ex02 but a full presenter-protagonist in ex05 and a caregiver with a sick parent in q08; 'Madeline' is the tired designer of the fullRead/ex04/ex06 yet also the detached advisor in Bonnie's text thread. The dense reuse of the same six names for shifting roles within one chapter reads as templated character-slotting a reader would notice.
